Power comes from the HiSilicon Kirin 8000 (7nm), which keeps everyday apps quick and handles popular games smoothly at sensible settings. The rear camera setup is 50 MP (wide) + 8 MP (ultrawide), and the high-resolution main sensor is the one you will lean on for daylight shots, which come out detailed. Battery capacity is 5,000mAh, which is a full-day size for most users, and 100W charging means top-ups are genuinely quick when you are in a hurry.

On the software side it runs HarmonyOS 4.2 (EMUI 14.2 global) (verified). It is aimed at buyers who want premium features without paying full flagship money. In Pakistan it is listed at Rs 112,800 (market price, checked 2026-09-30) — confirm the final price, variant and warranty with the seller before paying.
notes: Price is for the 12GB/256GB variant. No Google Mobile Services (uses Huawei AppGallery). Also supports 5W reverse wired charging.

software.software_notes: Huawei publishes no update-year promise. Runs EMUI 14.2 (HarmonyOS-based) with NO Google Play services — no Play Store, no Google apps; Huawei's AppGallery only. Clean software otherwise.

gaming.gaming_notes: With the Kirin 8000 and 12GB RAM, expect smooth high-setting gameplay in PUBG/BGMI; only the heaviest titles need a small step down from max.
